To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the PAHs in the SMC B molecular cloud are more abundant than the PAHs elsewhere in the Small Magellenic Cloud, that the PAH IR bands in the Small Magellanican Cloud are weaker than the PAH bands in the Milky Way, and that the IR band strengths of the PAHs are correlated with metallicity.

the infrared emission from intersteller dust in the Small and Large Magellanic Clouds is best explained using a mixture of carbonaceous and amorphous siliceous grains, and that the relative abundance of PAHs in the Small Magelanic Cloud is lower than in the Milky Way.

the IR emission from interstellar grains in the SMC is best explained by a model that includes a PAH population, and that the PAHs in the SMC have different IR band strengths than those found in the Milky Way.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (a) What is the dust composition in the Small Magellanics Cloud?
the following issues: (1) The dust properties in the SMC and its dependence on the environment.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PAHs in the SMC are very different than in the Milky Way.
the SMC Bar is a dusty region with a low PAH abundance and a PAH mixture with intrinsic IR band strengths different from those in the Milky Way.
the SMC is deficient in PAHs compared to the Milky Way, and the PAH abundance increases in molecular clouds.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PAH IR bands are a sensitive probe of the interstellar dust environment.
the PAHs in the SMC are very different in abundance and intrinsic IR band strengths from the Milky Way PAHs.
the IR emission from interstellar PAHs in the SMC is very different from the IR emission in our own Galaxy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SMC Bar and SMC B1 are different in the abundance of PAHs, as well as in the intrinsic IR band strengths of the PAH mixture.
the PAH IR emission bands are very sensitive to the environment and that the PAH band strengths are likely to vary with metallicity and/or environmental conditions.
the PAH abundances in the SMC and Milky Way differ significantly.
